agent.problem: The correct answer is the only choice in formal biblical wording, while the other two shift into modern phrasing, especially the offhand and exaggerated 'They will never face a hard day ever again.' The correct answer stands out instead of all three choices sounding alike.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

human.problem: 'My father was a wandering Aramean' brings in a new person without saying who he is. The text doesn't name him. He is commonly understood to be Jacob, who went down to Egypt few in number (Gen 46). The new-people rule asks Papa Dorin to say who someone is, but the leave-open rule asks him not to fill in what the text leaves open.
human.question: When a passage refers to an unnamed person whom other Scripture points to, like the wandering Aramean in Deuteronomy 26:5, should Papa Dorin name him (Jacob, with a reference like Gen 46:3-7)? Or should he leave him unnamed because the passage doesn't name him?
